summary:
Lunex is a lunar south-pole mission-planning tool that helps explore how location, terrain, and time affect potential landing-site conditions.

It combines NASA's LOLA elevation data with time-specific Sun and Earth observations from NASA/JPL Horizons. Users can explore three prepared locations: Shackleton Rim, de Gerlache Rim and Malapert Massif, select a point on the terrain map, and examine how surrounding terrain may affect sunlight and visibility of Earth.

Lunex also analyses observations across time to identify potential periods when both the Sun and Earth may be visible from a selected location.

Our goal is to make complex lunar terrain and visibility information easier to explore together, helping researchers and mission planners better understand the conditions that matter when evaluating future landing sites.
details:
Lunex brings together lunar terrain, celestial observations and time in one interactive mission-planning experience.

Users begin by selecting one of three prepared NASA LOLA Product 78 locations: Shackleton Rim, de Gerlache Rim or Malapert Massif. They can select a point directly on the high-resolution terrain map and explore its surroundings in 3D.

For the selected location, Lunex retrieves time-specific Sun and Earth observations from NASA/JPL Horizons. It samples the surrounding elevation data to build a local terrain-horizon profile and compares the celestial positions against that terrain. A full-day analysis also searches for potential periods when both the Sun and Earth may be visible.

The application combines a regional lunar map, elevation data, 360-degree terrain exploration, celestial observations and visibility timelines. This helps users understand how the surrounding landscape and observation time can affect mission planning.

We built Lunex using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, OpenLayers, GeoTIFF and proj4, integrating NASA datasets and APIs.

The terrain data uses a 5 m/pixel grid. NASA notes that much of this grid is interpolated, so pixel spacing should not be interpreted as measurement accuracy. Terrain coverage is also incomplete, and potential visibility windows remain provisional where the full horizon is unverified.

Lunex is a planning and visualization prototype, not a landing-safety certification, solar-power model or radio communications link-budget tool.
